races.name: Jenningsbet Over 200 Shops Nationwide Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with reasonable course form over 6f on Good, but her best work has come at 5f on similar surfaces; stepping up to the Brighton 6f asks her to reach her effort very late and she needs the pace to truly collapse in front of her.|
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last six starts, Love Alive has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 65 just edges this field of five — the main concern is that she remains winless in recent starts despite those placing efforts.

runners_data.name: Havana Jag
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will look to press for the lead from the off; Ashley Lewis (claiming 3lb) is a positive but his sim-going record (4/12, 0W3P) is modest and he has placed three times without converting, suggesting he may be vulnerable once challenged on the hill.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Jag has been a model of consistency, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going — the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Cape Toronada
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 3yo has strong credentials here — a winner over 6f on Good at Brighton course-distance, placed twice more on similar going (6/8 record), and William Carson rides with course authority; the 44-day break is the only mild caution but form held well last time out.|
runners_data.comment: Cape Toronada won two starts back but has finished fourth on her two most recent outings, and her speed rating of 54 leaves her well below the level needed to trouble these rivals. She has run over today's trip and going, and stall one is hers, but she heads into this ranked last of five on our figures.

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (p) for the first time on this surface and will be keen to go forward alongside Havana Jag; Scott Dixon's runner has a deeply disappointing record on Good-ish ground (2/15, 0W1P) and his one win came on Standard at 5f, making Brighton's fast turf a significant concern.|
runners_data.comment: Mister Moet caught the eye with a second two starts back and brings a win five starts back into the equation; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 132 lb from stall four, the 15-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh and ready.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Prominent-running filly wearing a visor (v) for Scott Dixon who also trains Mister Moet, adding a stable-pair dynamic to the race; her sim-going record (4/15, 0W0P) is the weakest in the field and she has not won in six recent starts, though she has been competitive enough to sit just off the pace and make a race of it in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Beach Partee has run over today's trip and going, holds a 62 rating against an official mark of 56, and returns fit on 21 days' rest from stall two — making him a live danger on these terms; the concern is he's winless in his last six starts.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Jag and Mister Moet are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead down Brighton's opening straight, creating a genuinely competitive pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. On Good to Firm ground at 6f on Brighton's undulating track — where the final climb rewards horses travelling comfortably — an honest early duel between these two risks burning both off before the business end. Cape Toronada and Beach Partee sit prominently and will be positioned just off the speed, while Love Alive works from off the pace at the back. This race shape — contested early, honest gallop into the hill — classically favours the prominent hold-and-pounce profile over the pure lead or deep hold-up position; horses who can sit just behind the duel and pounce as the pace-setters tire on the rise home are best served here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Aids Chasers
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Jag and Mister Moet genuinely contest the lead and burn each other off into the Brighton hill.
scenarios.body: The early duel between the two front-runners sets a demanding tempo that compromises both by the two-furlong marker, opening the door for those travelling within themselves just off the speed. Cape Toronada, with strong course-distance form on this going including a win at 6f on Good, is ideally positioned to swoop, and Beach Partee can also capitalise from the prominent group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner asserts dominance quickly and the other backs off, leaving a solo leader to control the pace.
scenarios.body: Should Havana Jag or Mister Moet blink first and cede the lead without a prolonged fight, the surviving leader is able to dictate a controlled gallop and save enough for the hill. Mister Moet's headgear (p) may help him assert early, but his poor Brighton sim-going record (2/15, 0W1P) is a concern if he gets to the front in isolation and must sustain it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly severe and Love Alive travels strongly from the back to reel in the field up the hill.
scenarios.body: Love Alive needs a genuinely strong pace to bring her hold-up style into play over 6f, and while she has 3yo course form over this trip on Good, her flat-track form at 5f makes the step up in trip and course demands here a slight ask. A true burning pace could bring her into it late, but her sim-going record of 6/12 with no wins makes this an upside scenario rather than a likely outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the race is run at a moderate, tactical tempo with the field bunched.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over 6f at Brighton would compress the field and make it a sprint up the hill, potentially flattening the formlines. In this scenario the most unexposed or highest-rated animal on the day could prevail in a messy finish, but this shape requires both Havana Jag and Mister Moet to show uncharacteristic restraint — unlikely given their profiles.

watchPoints.text: Havana Jag and Mister Moet — watch the first two furlongs closely; if they engage in a prolonged duel the pace could be genuinely severe, materially changing the chance of the front two at the business end.

Cape Toronada — Carson's mount will be keen to stalk the pace and if she gets clear daylight approaching the final furlong on the hill she is the most likely beneficiary of any pace collapse given her excellent course-distance record.
Mister Moet's hood — the headgear is worn for the first time here; watch in the early stages whether it helps him assert or whether it sends him forward too aggressively and costs him at the finish.

Love Alive — Alistair Rawlinson drops her back in the field; watch whether she gets a clear run up the inside on the Brighton camber or whether the small field compresses and blocks her late challenge.

Beach Partee — the Dixon yard saddles two runners; if Mister Moet burns out early, note whether Beach Partee receives any positive tactical ride from Tyler Heard or whether the race simply gets away from her.

races.name: Jenningsbet In Deal Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for Dylan Cunha who sets the tempo throughout; Good to Firm is fine on going, but poor recent form (0,0,0,6,6,5) at this trip and 3-day turnaround on a fresh surface raises serious reservations about winning potential despite the positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with three unplaced efforts among them, Aspire To Glory is hard to fancy on recent evidence; he returns quickly just three days after his latest fifth, though he has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall one.

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's seven-year-old has headgear (p) and genuine hold-up credentials — true closer whose natural position is off the back, pushed into the midfield representation purely by the volume of rear-runners in this field; five placed runs from 15 similar-going starts show she can operate on Good ground but winning has been elusive.
runners_data.comment: Celebrating Ethel won six starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a live each-way squeak from stall three; the concern is that she has been unplaced in her last five starts since that victory.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John Gallagher who has repeatedly struggled to convert — a single place in 15 similar-going runs signals consistency concerns; 18-day break and blinkers (b) could sharpen, but form figures of 1,6,0,5,4,0 suggest this is a horse to oppose rather than support even in a contested lead scenario.
runners_data.comment: First Encounter shaped with promise when winning in recent starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating marking him down as the one to beat from stall 4; the risk is that he has gone unplaced twice since that victory.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sign
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes over on Mark Pattinson's eight-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has solid course-track experience; the best recent placing-form figure in the race (2nd last time over 7f on Good) and the most good-going placed runs of any prominent type make this a horse to respect if the pace hotpot weakens.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Rainbow Sign at least showed a glimpse of ability with a second two starts back, though a seventh last time out is harder to ignore; he has experience over today's trip and going, but a mark of 47 and mid-field ranking leave him with plenty to prove from stall 8.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll fields a second runner in hold-up mode via apprentice Molly Gunn (5lb), and River Wharfe's recent run in similar going (5th, 8f, Good) is the most relevant recent form evidence; tongue-tie on, but needs a true gallop to close from the rear and the likely controlled fractions are a concern.
runners_data.comment: River Wharfe has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 52, shapes as a leading danger from stall seven, fit on just 16 days' recovery — yet winless in his last six starts, that persistent inability to convert remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Carroll's third string on the day, this four-year-old is a natural off-the-pace type whose low OR (41) and uniformly poor recent figures (6,10,8,8,9) suggest chronic under-performance; Cieren Fallon is a positive booking but the horse's form pattern makes it difficult to construct a winning scenario regardless of pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-to-tail finishes, Rock Master is hard to fancy here — ranked eighth of nine on our figures. He has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests he's ready, but the evidence of late offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old has the most consistent placed form in the race — four places from six similar-going starts including two runner-up finishes at this trip and going under Owen Lewis (5lb); genuine hold-up profile sits naturally in the rear and is not compromised by redistribution, making this the most credible late finisher if tempo is sufficient.
runners_data.comment: Rovinia arrives here in solid nick after consecutive runner-up finishes, and having run over today's trip and going she's well placed on conditions. Carrying 135 lb from stall five, she's yet to score in recent starts but her consistency makes her our preferred pick at a rating of 52.

runners_data.name: Sangara
runners_data.note: Sheena West's four-year-old returns after a 305-day layoff flagged with a tendency to fade in the finish — those two factors in combination make it very hard to assess current condition; Good-ground form is weak (12th and 10th from similar conditions) and the absence warning is a significant betting risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 305 days off, Sangara faces a stiff ask, though a third two starts back shows she can hit the frame and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Skyolaire
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins's lightly-raced three-year-old is a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the cluster of closers in this field; 45-day break and no trainer activity in the last 14 days are both cautionary flags, and while the form figures have been improving incrementally, the style-fit discount and the positional compromise combine to suppress expectations here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a string of mid-to-rear finishes, Skyolaire is hard to fancy as the lowest-rated runner in the field, though she has run over today's distance and going before and draws from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pressure expected, will dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground around Brighton's undulating mile. First Encounter and Rainbow Sign will push for prominent positions behind, creating a small cluster chasing the leader but unlikely to seriously disrupt the tempo. The race shape points clearly toward horses who can travel in touch from off the pace and produce a sustained finish — hold-up horses with genuine staying ability and proven good-ground form are best positioned here. Skyolaire, Rock Master, and Celebrating Ethel are true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more off-the-pace runners than the visual map can accommodate at the rear, with River Wharfe and Rovinia the most likely to secure their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire To Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory leads uncontested and sets an honest but not suicidal gallop, allowing the front to dictate.
scenarios.body: Aspire To Glory bowls along in front with no rival willing to commit to chasing hard, and the tempo stays modest enough that the leader retains enough energy to hold on turning for home; on Good to Firm Brighton ground a controlled front-runner is notoriously difficult to dislodge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is strong enough through the middle mile to set up a fast-finishing challenge from the rear.
scenarios.body: River Wharfe or Rovinia, sitting patiently in the rear-to-midfield pack, get a clear run rounding the home bend and produce a sustained late effort on the fast ground; Rovinia's recent placed form at this trip and going gives her the profile to take advantage of a genuine pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter or Rainbow Sign push Aspire To Glory hard early and the front group sets a pace that leaves the leader vulnerable.
scenarios.body: A sustained mid-race battle up front drains Aspire To Glory before the final descent, handing the advantage to a prominent racer who tracked slightly off the leader and picks up the pieces; Rainbow Sign's recent placed form and Pat Cosgrave's Brighton experience make this profile credible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Redistributed Types
scenarios.trigger: If the race is truly falsely run and the redistributed hold-up horses trapped in midfield find an unexpected gap.
scenarios.body: Skyolaire, Rock Master, or Celebrating Ethel would need to overcome their forced positional compromise and produce better form than their recent figures suggest; this scenario is discounted sharply given all three carry STYLE_FIT flags and are racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Aspire To Glory sets the early tempo unchallenged — watch whether any of First Encounter or Rainbow Sign commit to chasing before halfway, as the absence of a pursuer is the single biggest factor enabling a front-runner's victory on this track.

Rovinia is the hold-up runner with the strongest recent placed form, but Owen Lewis's 5lb claim needs to be offset against whether the pace is strong enough through the middle sections to create the gap she needs on the home turn.

Tony Carroll runs three horses (Celebrating Ethel, River Wharfe, Rock Master) — stable form is moderate (3 wins from 32 in 14 days) and multiple stable entries can create tactical interference among hold-up runners all needing the same late-race gap.

Sangara's 305-day absence combined with the fade-in-finish flag makes her a significant unknown — monitor pre-race market movement as any sustained support would suggest a stable that has done meaningful work at home unseen by public form.

Brighton's home turn punishes runners who are checked or blocked wide — Skyolaire, Rock Master and Celebrating Ethel, all mapped away from their natural position, are most vulnerable to losing ground at the critical point of the race.

races.name: Sapporo Japanese Premium Lager Brighton Mile Challenge Handicap Stakes (For The Brighton Mile Challenge Trophy)

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Won twice at this 1m trip on Good, controls the race from the front under Carmichael with a STYLE_FIT note suggesting she's at her best when allowed to dictate — conditions here are near-ideal and the uncontested lead is a significant asset.
runners_data.comment: Silca Bay is the one to beat here: a winner last time out and again three starts back, he has experience over today's trip and going, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh. The 143 lb burden is the one query.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this consistent sort who has winning form at 1m on Good; four placed efforts in similar company suggest she travels well prominently and is effective when a pace-setter softens up the field ahead of her.
runners_data.comment: Sea Suite arrives in excellent nick — a runner-up two starts back and again last time out, 12 days ago — and has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is whether he can finally convert his consistency into victory carrying 142 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Newfangled
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's five-year-old has a natural desire to race up with the pace, though the competitive early positions in this field mean she is likely to find herself racing in a more restrained role than she'd prefer — her best form has come when dictating or racing handy, so the compromise may blunt her.

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: An 86-day absence is the chief concern for Oli Rix's three-year-old, who drops back from a poor effort in his last run; his hold-up style needs a strong pace to exploit and Jonny Peate will be working against the grain of this race shape.
runners_data.comment:
Winless in her last five starts, though a second three starts back offers a flicker of hope; she returns after 86 days off, has run over today's trip and going, and carries 135 lb from stall one, making her a each-way longshot at best from midfield.

Winless in her last five starts, though a second three starts back offers a flicker of encouragement; she returns after 86 days

runners_data.name: Tex
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good recently and has placed form on similar going, but steps up slightly in class here; a true hold-up horse who is reliant on Pat Cosgrave finding a clean passage through — the sustainable pace set by Silca Bay is the critical obstacle to his chance.
runners_data.comment: Tex bounced back to winning form two starts back and, carrying 133 lb from stall six, he brings both distance and going experience to the table — the chief concern is whether that disappointing ninth last time out signals a return to inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Northern Empire
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has a win on his CV but has struggled for consistency, showing a big swing in form; Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) settles him prominently, which is a positional strength, though his trainer's 14-day strike rate of 10/34 is solid context.
runners_data.comment: Northern Empire has managed just one win in his last five starts, finishing fifth last time out after a run of poor efforts, and our figures rank him eighth of nine in the field. He has run over today's trip and a trainer striking at 29% recently offers slim encouragement, but the form line makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Four-run career with placed form on Good at the mile trip gives Jack Callan something to work with; races prominently and is unexposed at this level for Charlie Johnston, making him an interesting contender if he travels into the race with his usual freshness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Glen Nevis faces a stiff task here; that said, he has run over today's trip and going before, returns fit at 25 days, and a third two starts back shows he can threaten the frame on his day.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's four-year-old is a natural front-runner by inclination but must concede ground positionally in this race shape as Silca Bay commands the lead; Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) will have to adapt the ride, and the STYLE_FIT discount is real — his best form has come when he gets his own way up front.
runners_data.comment: Play Me won two starts back but has finished fifth on his most recent outing, and while he has run over today's trip and going, a mark of 64 and a return to form are both needed to trouble the principals from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old has finished placed multiple times on Good ground at this sort of trip, including over 8f; races from the back and is dependent on generous fractions materialising — his consistency is notable but the tactical picture here does not point his way.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Giant has been placed third two starts back and second three starts back, but eighth last time out is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and 11 days between runs suggests freshness, yet his figures make him hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Silca Bay is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, is set to control this mile from the front at a sustainable, uncontested clip on Good to Firm ground. Sea Suite, Northern Empire, and Glen Nevis will press for prominent positions just behind, creating a small cluster of sit-and-track types that will define the race's middle section. The hold-up runners — Here I Bow, Tex, and Giant — will be last to settle and rely entirely on a meaningful early pace to generate the run-home they need; with Silca Bay dictating an honest but unforced tempo, that late zip may not materialise. This race shape unambiguously favours horses racing prominently in behind the leader, able to pounce in the final quarter-mile without needing a strong pace collapse. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Newfangled and Play Me are genuine prominent racers in reality, but Sea Suite, Northern Empire, and Glen Nevis are most likely to actually hold those coveted early positions given the pressure ahead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silca Bay Leads, Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay dictates an unchallenged, honest tempo and the prominent trackers cannot sustain their challenge to the line.
scenarios.body: Silca Bay sets her own fractions from the front with Oliver Carmichael riding confidently, and the hold-up horses find insufficient pace to reel her in late. Horses sitting second or third — particularly Sea Suite or Glen Nevis — are best placed to inherit the race if Silca Bay ties up, but she remains the dominant force.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pounce Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay's lead is pegged back in the final two furlongs and a prominent tracker swoops past cleanly.
scenarios.body: Sea Suite or Glen Nevis, travelling comfortably just off the pace, accelerates past a tiring Silca Bay as the undulations of Brighton take their toll on the leader. This suits horses who have the class to travel into a race and finish with purpose rather than needing a strong gallop to set them alight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay pushes the pace harder than expected, creating a genuine gallop that opens the race up for late closers.
scenarios.body: Tex or Giant, racing further back, gets a run of daylight in the straight and picks off tiring rivals under strong riding. This shape requires a materially faster early tempo than Silca Bay has shown willingness to set, making it an against-the-odds outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If something disrupts early order — a slow start, a squeeze for position — and the race breaks up into atypical running positions.
scenarios.body: A compressed midfield bunch with no clear leader could produce a surprise result, favouring a horse like Giant or Here I Bow who benefits from an unusual shape that negates natural positional disadvantages. Given Silca Bay's straightforward front-running profile and clear stall draw, genuine disruption to the shape is unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Silca Bay's uncontested lead is the race's defining factor — watch whether Oliver Carmichael allows her to stride on or deliberately anchors the tempo, as the former makes her very hard to catch, the latter opens the door for Sea Suite or Glen Nevis.

Sea Suite and Glen Nevis will both seek prominent positions just off the pace; if they crowd each other early in the straight, one or both could be checked at the critical moment — watch their positioning as they round the final bend.

Here I Bow returns from 86 days off and has shown nothing threatening in recent runs — if he travels unexpectedly well early, it signals freshness that could make him a live threat late, but any sluggish start confirms he is out of the picture.

Tex won over 7f last time but has a poor record over 8f on Standout/AW — if Brighton's undulations expose that stamina question, he may fade when asked for his effort despite Cosgrave's positive booking.

Play Me and Newfangled, both natural front-runners displaced to a midfield role by the race shape, are worth monitoring for signs of frustration or awkward travelling — if either fails to settle, it compounds their already compromised tactical position.

races.name: Monty Bennetts 18th Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Annexation
runners_data.note: Consistent 10yo with good-ground form and multiple top-four finishes at this sort of trip, but his natural role is as a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward in the map — in a race with only one pace-setter he may struggle to produce his best from a position closer to the action than he'd prefer.
runners_data.comment: Annexation showed his best recent form when runner-up two starts back, and having run over today's trip and going, he arrives here on a competitive mark and retains strong claims as the top-rated runner in a field of six, albeit yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: It's Life
runners_data.note: The most interesting form angle here is a recent 1m win on Good ground, and trainer Kathy Burke is in smart form (T14: 3/4), but this horse's instinct is to race at the back of the field and in a slowly-run race off Beryl's Girl's lead, getting a clear run late may prove difficult.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out is the one flag worth raising for It's Life, though four starts either side of that success read 11 days ago show a patchy profile, and she ranks fifth of six on our figures — hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: West Hill Rosie
runners_data.note: Has a tendency to fade in the finish which is a notable concern on quick ground over 1m2f, and after 45 days off she faces a fitness question; her best form has come when racing close to the pace but her recent records at Brighton-type tracks show she has struggled to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with the highlight a third last time out, West Hill Rosie faces a stiff task as the bottom-rated runner here; 45 days off and 131 lb are further negatives, though she does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a strong recent form profile — two wins and four places from her last 12 runs on Good ground, all over 1m — stepping up slightly in trip here but the consistent placing record suggests she handles pressure and is among the most straightforward profiles in the race to trust off a moderate pace.
runners_data.comment: Buckland Belle arrives on the back of a win last time out, with a second two starts back and strong recent form that marks her out as a genuine threat here; carrying 130 lb from stall two is the weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Has a win at 9f on Soft and placed form at similar distances, though his good-ground record over slightly longer trips is patchy (sim-going: 9/15, 1W1P); Rob Hornby takes the ride for the powerful Charlie Johnston yard and the step into an end-to-end pace scenario is manageable if he travels fluidly.
runners_data.comment: Port Darwin won three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while 25 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh at a handy 130 lb; the concern is two consecutive fifth-placed finishes since that win.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race and therefore the sole pace-setter; her Brighton win over 1m2f on Good is directly relevant and Rhys Clutterbuck retains the ride, but her recent form string (-46617) shows limited consistency and the pressure of making all the running for the full trip on quick ground is a genuine stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Beryl's Girl showed she can win at this level, scoring one start back, and she has experience of today's trip and going — stamping her as a genuine threat from stall one at 130 lb; the worry is that seventh on her latest outing leaves her needing to bounce back sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Beryl's Girl is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, and with no rival willing or able to press her from the front, she is set to coast into an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating 1m2f. The remainder of the field — Annexation, It's Life, and West Hill Rosie — are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are more closers than the rear can accommodate; none of them are natural stalkers and their true role is to come late. Buckland Belle and Port Darwin are the best-credentialled finishers at the trip and represent the most genuine midfield-to-closing threats once Beryl's Girl sets her own tempo. With one horse dictating a solo, sustainable gallop on quick ground, this race shape strongly favours confirmed hold-up runners with a powerful late surge — horses capable of closing ground efficiently on a surface that rewards travelling well and finishing hard.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beryl's Girl Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beryl's Girl bowls clear from the off and the pursuing pack lack the organised early pace to close the gap before the straight.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl dictates every fraction at her own tempo on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival prepared to take her on, she is able to control the race fully through the final bend; her 1m2f win at Brighton over this trip is a key form reference. Horses who can pick up off a genuine lead and sustain momentum into the closing stages — Buckland Belle and Port Darwin — are the profiles best placed to reel her in or challenge close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Finishers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to compromise Beryl's Girl's stamina in the straight and closers arrive in a rush.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl's solo lead on quick ground may expose her stamina over 1m2f if she has gone slightly too freely early, allowing the hold-up horses to close with a collective surge in the final two furlongs. Buckland Belle, who holds excellent form at 1m on Good ground with multiple placed and winning runs, is the profile to capitalise, with Port Darwin also a credible late beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Raider From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If one hold-up horse tracks Beryl's Girl closer than expected and delivers a sustained challenge from two furlongs out rather than a last-gasp finish.
scenarios.body: Port Darwin, who has won at 9f on Soft and placed at similar trips, is capable of travelling prominently enough from a midfield position to peg back a front-runner if the pace is modest; this scenario suits a horse that can travel smoothly in the slipstream and kick decisively. Buckland Belle's consistent placing record suggests she could fulfil the same role if covered up just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses — Annexation or It's Life — manage to find their natural off-the-pace berth and the race develops into a true test of late speed.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Annexation or It's Life racing in their genuine role at the back and delivering a sweeping late run, but both are mapped out of their natural position and face an uphill task in a field that does not generate enough early pace to set up a true late sprint. It's Life's recent 1m win on Good is the one form reference that could justify inclusion, but the tactical conditions make this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Beryl's Girl is the only pace-setter in a six-runner field — if she bowls clear unchallenged she could prove very hard to reel in on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Brighton, and any horse unable to make significant ground by the two-furlong pole is likely beaten.

West Hill Rosie's tendency to fade in the finish, combined with 45 days off the track and a trainer with no recent runners (T14: 0/0), makes her vulnerable in a race that may test stamina on quick ground — watch for her to drop away turning into the straight.

Annexation and It's Life are both natural rear-runners operating out of their preferred role in this race shape; if Beryl's Girl sets a truly modest tempo, neither may generate the momentum to launch a meaningful late challenge from midfield.
Kathy Turner's T14 strike rate of 3/4 with It's Life is worth monitoring — a short-priced yard angle on a recent winner can attract market support that moves the price significantly before the off.

Buckland Belle steps up from 1m to 1m2f for the first time; watch how she travels in the first half of the race — if she settles comfortably behind Beryl's Girl she is the most likely challenger, but if she races keenly tracking the leader the extra two furlongs could find her out.

races.name: Jenningsbet "we Love Brighton Racecourse" 'confined' Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist with nine wins to his name; has placed five times from nine runs on similar going but recent form shows nothing better than fifth, and 22 days since his last run is unremarkable; on a track that rarely rewards pure closers in a steady-pace race, his chance is conditional on something going wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Redredrobin has run over today's trip and going, arrives 22 days fresh, and a speed rating of 68 puts her ahead of most rivals on these terms — yet she's winless in her last five starts, and that persistent inability to convert remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: The Organiser
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer trained by Mark Pattinson; Pat Cosgrave takes the ride and brings quality, but this horse has only found the frame once in four turf starts on similar going and has been disappointing on AW recently; needs a strongly-run race to bring his finishing kick into play.
runners_data.comment: Placed three starts back and keeping on consistently in recent outings, The Organiser has experience over today's trip and going, and at 136 lb from stall 9, our rating has him joint-top of this field — winless in his last five, but the form profile makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished second on six of his last seven starts on good ground, including multiple seven-furlong Brighton-style trips; Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) keeps the weight competitive and this horse is arguably the most reliably placed in the field for the likely race shape; the lack of a win becomes the main concern.
runners_data.comment: Havana Mojito has been placed second in four consecutive starts yet remains winless in recent starts, so the ability to convert is a question mark; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to go again.

runners_data.name: Berning Hot
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's four-year-old has genuine hold-up instincts that are his natural mode; redistribution to midfield on the map reflects an overcrowded rear contingent rather than a change in how he will race — his best Brighton-type form came when getting a clear run late, and a leisurely King Cherry gallop makes that harder to engineer.
runners_data.comment: Berning Hot is winless in her last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; she has experience over today's trip and going, returns on a quick 13-day turnaround, and draws stall one carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' three-year-old is the lone front-runner and Rob Hornby should have him bowling along without a challenger beside him; going form is modest (0W0P from four similar-ground starts) but the tactical advantage of unopposed lead on Good to Firm Brighton is significant and not to be underestimated.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, King Cherry nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table and is lightly weighted at 133 lb from stall 3, with our rating of 63 nudging ahead of his official mark — the concern is that his recent string of mid-field finishes offers little confidence of a sudden turnaround.

runners_data.name: Quite Sweet
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's four-year-old carries a warning flag for fading in finishes, and her recent form on AW (no win on similar turf going from nine attempts) does little to inspire; a true hold-up type shuffled into a midfield map position because the rear is crowded, meaning she is unlikely to get the clean late run her style demands — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Quite Sweet has managed just the one win in her last five starts, finishing ninth most recently, and her figures place her seventh of nine in this field; she has run over today's trip and going before, which at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Viking Glory
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old has placed on good ground and shaped with some promise at six furlongs, but stepping to seven furlongs for Brighton brings a stamina question; Cieren Fallon is a significant booking and the trainer has been in form (13/57 over 14 days), so the jockey angle warrants noting even if the hold-up style is awkward in a slow-paced race.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and again five starts back, Viking Glory brings genuine placed form into this, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour — the chief concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: A six-year-old genuine hold-up performer trained by Tony Carroll alongside stablemate Quite Sweet; naturally races from the rear but the overcrowded hold-up division forces him forward on the map — at OR 46 and having raced mostly at five and six furlongs recently, both the trip and the race shape look against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Daley T showed a glimmer three runs back with a third but has otherwise disappointed, and being ranked eighth of nine on our figures makes him hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip and going before, and stall two is his lot at 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Miraflores
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's four-year-old comes to Brighton without a win from 14 starts on similar going and has finished no better than fourth in that sample; a natural come-from-behind type whose redistribution to midfield signals the difficulty of securing a true rear position — OR 45 and zero wins in similar conditions makes it hard to make a case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fourth in that sequence, Miraflores faces a stiff ask here — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and 15 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: King Cherry is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on a flat Brighton seven-furlong track with Good to Firm conditions underfoot, should control this race from the off at a sustainable, uncontested gallop under Rob Hornby. Behind him, Havana Mojito is the most likely prominent horse to press or sit just off the pace, having finished second in five of his last seven starts and showing strong course-compatible form. The hold-up contingent is unusually large for a nine-runner field: Berning Hot, Quite Sweet, Daley T and Miraflores are all genuine come-from-behind types but the map cannot accommodate all of them at the rear, meaning several will inevitably race closer to the pace than they would prefer, diluting their effectiveness. With King Cherry dictating a controlled tempo and no genuine pace rival to force a truly genuine gallop, this race shape favours prominent racers who can sit within two lengths of the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than horses needing a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Cherry Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry leads from the front and Havana Mojito settles into second without applying early pressure, creating a controlled, measured gallop.
scenarios.body: King Cherry sets a comfortable tempo around the Brighton contours and kicks for home turning in, with the honest, prominent-running Havana Mojito the horse best placed to reel him in having tracked the fractions throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fair-to-strong and Havana Mojito or a hold-up type gets a clear run from just off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Brighton's long rising finish can blunt the leaders if the early pace is honest enough, giving a horse like Havana Mojito or a prominent racer positioned just behind the leader a winning surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Gets Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is unexpectedly strong and the field strings out, leaving genuine closers with daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated tempo from King Cherry, perhaps pushed into it by Havana Mojito, could set the race up for a true hold-up performer if they get a clean late run on the stands side.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead and the race breaks up chaotically, leaving no horse able to dominate.
scenarios.body: With several redistributed hold-up types forced nearer the pace than ideal, a fractious early pace could see them interfere with one another and produce a messy race that benefits a fresh-legged outlier.

watchPoints.text: Watch King Cherry's early lead — if Rob Hornby is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged through the first three furlongs, the controlled tempo could be slow enough to make him very hard to catch turning into Brighton's straight.

Havana Mojito is the form horse in the race but has now finished second six times in recent months without winning; watch whether Ashley Lewis elects to go past King Cherry early or sit and wait, as the timing of that move will be decisive.

Quite Sweet's stamina warning flag is significant — if she hits the front early in the straight she may not sustain it; watch for William Carson positioning her more prominently than her natural style suggests, which could compromise her finishing effort.

Viking Glory is the shortest-priced hold-up type with a live jockey booking in Cieren Fallon; watch how much daylight he gets on the rail turning for home, as Brighton's camber can trap horses on the inside without a gap.

With four horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types (Berning Hot, Quite Sweet, Daley T, Miraflores), watch the first two furlongs for signs of crowding or interference in the rear pack as genuine closers compete for the same ground.

races.name: Free Race Replays On Attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Pop Dancer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Tony Carroll at OR 61, carrying top weight after a 339-day absence — the long layoff is the single biggest question mark, and if rustiness costs her in the early pace battle, her natural advantage is forfeited entirely.
runners_data.comment: Pop Dancer showed real ability when winning and finishing second in his recent starts, and has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is whether he retains that form after a 339-day absence.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Dual trainer yard-mate of Pop Dancer under the in-form William Carson, returning on just 29 days; his recent Brighton win over 6f on good ground is directly relevant and he is the most likely of the three pace-setters to sustain his effort to the line if he can escape the early scrimmage.
runners_data.comment: Kento brings solid recent form — placed third, third, and second in his last three starts, with a win four starts back — and has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the main risk is whether he can convert that consistency into an overdue victory.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over on this prominent-to-hold-up sprinter who won over 5f on good ground 21 days ago; the visor goes on and his sim-going record of 8/15 is workmanlike, but his best chance lies in benefiting from the pace war unfolding ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and back on familiar distance and going, Secret Handsheikh arrives here on a pleasing 21-day break, fit and primed. Carrying 135 lb from stall seven, the fifth last time out is a minor concern, but his profile warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: The blinkered hold-up operator for the Cook & Bridger yard, ridden by the 3lb-claiming Ryan Kavanagh; his best form shows two seconds at 5-6f on good ground but his sim-going record of 9/15 with zero wins is a red flag, and he needs the pace to be truly punishing to close the gap in time.
runners_data.comment: Faustus has been placed twice in his last six starts — second last time out and second three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating putting him narrowly top-rated; the worry is he remains winless in recent starts and must prove he can convert.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated of the three lead-biased horses at OR 51 under Alistair Rawlinson for Michael Appleby; two wins on similar going are a positive but his recent sequence of 5-5-5-5 finishes suggests he is often outpaced in the closing stages when the pressure is on, making him the most vulnerable of the leading trio late on.

runners_data.name: Titus Thor
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is a severe negative in a race where the pace will already be extreme; his going record here of 3/7 with no wins or places at 5-6f on similar ground makes him unlikely to land a blow regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Titus Thor heads here ranked last on our figures and rated below his official mark — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and a 33-day break at least means he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a blinkered headgear entry under the 3lb claimer Christian Howarth; zero wins from 15 sim-going runs and a form string featuring a 12th last time out suggest he needs everything to fall perfectly for him to get involved, and the pace scenario would need to be extreme for his closing run to be meaningful.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a third two runs back her only encouragement, Coast faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 122 lb — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a small ratings edge offers slim consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Pop Dancer, Kento, and Starsong all want to lead, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for the rail and a strong early gallop on this sharp Brighton 5½f on good-to-firm ground. With three confirmed front-runners fighting for position from the off, the pace is unlikely to be controlled — it will be contested and honest from the first stride, putting stamina and finishing resolution at a premium by the time the field reaches the pronounced downhill finish. Secret Handsheikh and Faustus, the two hold-up types, will be able to track the carnage from behind and are the primary beneficiaries if the pace burns the leaders out in the closing stages. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners with a late kick, as the front rank is almost certain to tie itself in knots early, eroding their finishing reserves before the final furlong descent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Pop Dancer, Kento, and Starsong fight vigorously for early position and the pace is genuinely fierce through the first two furlongs, the front-runners will drain each other before the dip.
scenarios.body: The contest devolves into an end-to-end sprint that leaves the leaders hollow in the closing stages, allowing horses with tactical cover to deliver a late thrust down the hill. This scenario rewards runners who race with restraint in the early stages and still possess the finishing speed to capitalise as the pace-setters fold.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners establishes an early advantage unchallenged while the others fail to match strides or are restrained.
scenarios.body: A single leader controls the tempo at a measured but honest gallop, conserving enough to sustain the run to the line and repel closers whose momentum is blunted by a pace that never truly gets away from them. Kento, fresh from a recent win and with course-applicable form, is best placed to seize and hold this initiative if connections allow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Thrives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to neutralise pure front-runners but not sustained long enough for true hold-up horses to fully close.
scenarios.body: A prominent runner sitting just off the early battle emerges as the compromise winner, picking up the pieces when the leading trio weaken without needing to come from as far back as the hold-up horses. Secret Handsheikh, racing from a prominent position under Cieren Fallon, could exploit this middle-ground shape given a strong recent win on comparable going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Reach
scenarios.trigger: If the pace settles after initial jostling and a manageable gallop allows the front rank to recover, negating the hold-up horses' finishing run.
scenarios.body: The leaders control the tempo and the hold-up horses — Faustus and Coast — find the task simply too far as they fail to generate enough momentum through the field in time. A tactical, controlled race suits those racing handily, leaving the deepest closers stranded.

watchPoints.text: Pop Dancer's 339-day absence is the critical factor — watch whether she travels fluently in the early pace battle or shows signs of ring-rust, which would immediately transform the race dynamic for the other two front-runners.

If Kento or Pop Dancer force Starsong to concede the lead early, watch whether Starsong drops back sharply through the field — his recent finishing record suggests he burns out when he cannot control his own pace.

Secret Handsheikh's visor application under Cieren Fallon is a significant headgear angle — watch how sharply he travels in the first furlong, as a strong early move from off the pace could position him perfectly for the Brighton descent.

Faustus's claiming jockey Ryan Kavanagh must judge the pace perfectly — if he commits too early chasing the leaders, Faustus's hold-up profile is wasted; watch whether he is given a patient ride through the field.

With three front-runners at similar OR levels (61/59/51), watch the draw and the initial strides — whichever of Pop Dancer, Kento, or Starsong breaks quickest will define whether this is a pure pace war or a more controlled race, reshaping the value of every other runner accordingly.
